definition: A simple auxiliary classifier trained on a model's internal representations to test whether specific information (like syntactic structure) is encoded in those representations.
details: Probing classifiers are a common interpretability research tool for investigating what kinds of linguistic or semantic knowledge different layers of a language model have learned to encode.
story: Think of a hiker descending a foggy hill in the dark, taking small steps and feeling for the steepest way down. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. It is the same loop you use to learn anything: try, miss, correct, try again. Skill, for a model, is just error pushed down until it is small enough to ignore. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Probing Classifier.
